strategies.title: Fix your model and effort at session start
strategies.what_it_changes: Pick one model and effort level before work starts and keep them for the whole session; route any cheaper sub-task to a subagent instead of switching the parent mid-session.
strategies.expected_benefit: Avoids rebuilding the whole cached prefix on every mid-session model or effort change.
strategies.drawback: Locks you to one model and effort choice for the session; a genuine need to escalate mid-task means starting a new session instead of switching in place.
strategies.reversibility: Fully reversible, it is a habit, not a config change.
strategies.how_measured: behavior.model_switch_session_share is the share of your recent sessions that ran more than one model or effort value.
strategies.if_you_say_no: Each mid-session switch keeps rebuilding your cached prefix from zero at full price.

strategies.title: Shrink the always-loaded startup floor
strategies.what_it_changes: Diet CLAUDE.md to hard rules only, move rarely-used rules into path-scoped .claude/rules/ so they load only when a matching file is touched, and disable plugins and MCP servers you do not use.
strategies.expected_benefit: Cuts the fixed startup floor that gets re-read at cache-read price on every call in the session.
strategies.drawback: Moving a rule out of the always-loaded file means it stops applying to files that never match its new path scope; a rule that was silently always-on can silently stop firing.
strategies.how_measured: instruction.startup_floor_share is first-request tokens divided by everything the session reads.
strategies.if_you_say_no: The floor keeps being paid, at cache-read price, on every call for the life of the session.

strategies.title: Route cheap sub-tasks to a subagent, not a model switch
strategies.what_it_changes: When a step calls for a cheaper model, spawn a subagent for it instead of switching the parent session's model or effort in place.
strategies.expected_benefit: Keeps the parent session's cache intact while still using a cheaper model where it genuinely fits.
strategies.drawback: Subagents always use the 5 minute cache TTL, even on a subscription, so heavy subagent use pays more cache-write premium than parent-session work would.
strategies.how_measured: Same behavior.model_switch_session_share signal as the fixed-parent-model card, read as a routing habit rather than a config change.
strategies.if_you_say_no: Switches keep happening in the parent session, rebuilding its cache from zero each time.

strategies.title: Turn off git instructions you never use
strategies.what_it_changes: Set includeGitInstructions: false in settings if Claude Code is never asked to draft commits or PRs, removing the built-in git workflow instructions from what loads every session.
strategies.expected_benefit: Removes instructions you never use from the fixed context that every call re-reads.
strategies.drawback: If you ever do ask Claude to commit or open a PR, the built-in workflow guidance is gone and results get less consistent; the settings edit itself also costs one cache rebuild the next time it loads.
strategies.reversibility: Fully reversible, flip the setting back.
strategies.how_measured: instruction.startup_floor_share signals a heavy floor; this card is a check on whether an unused built-in feature is part of it. The profile carries no direct git-usage signal, so this is a coarse gate, not a precise detection.
strategies.if_you_say_no: The built-in git instructions keep loading on every session whether or not you use them.

strategies.title: Confirm MCP tool search is on
strategies.what_it_changes: Check that ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH has not been turned off; with several plugins and MCP servers installed, tool-search deferral is what keeps their tool schemas out of the always-loaded context.
strategies.expected_benefit: Keeps unused MCP tool definitions out of the fixed prompt instead of loading every schema up front.
strategies.drawback: Tool search adds one extra round trip the first time a deferred tool is actually called.
strategies.reversibility: Fully reversible, it is a check, not a change.
strategies.how_measured: environment.plugin_count from the profile; more installed plugins and MCP servers means more schemas are at stake if deferral is off.
strategies.if_you_say_no: If tool search was disabled some other way, every tool schema loads on every call whether it is used or not.

strategies.title: Keep waits under the cache TTL
strategies.what_it_changes: Recommend-only: background long waits with a completion callback instead of leaving the session idle past the active cache TTL (5 minutes on an API key, 1 hour on a subscription).
strategies.expected_benefit: Avoids paying full cache-write price again after the prefix goes cold.
strategies.drawback: This is advice only, no config change; and the 1 hour TTL is not free either, a write at the 1 hour TTL bills at 2x base input against 0.1x for a read, a real premium paid for the longer window, so a wait that stays under the TTL beats waiting past it and rebuilding.
strategies.reversibility: Not applicable, this is a workflow habit, not a setting.
strategies.how_measured: behavior.idle_gap_shares is the share of gaps between calls that ran past the session's active cache TTL.
strategies.if_you_say_no: Every gap that outlives the TTL means the next call rebuilds the prefix from a write instead of a 0.1x read.

strategies.title: Prefer a fresh session at real phase boundaries
strategies.what_it_changes: At a real phase boundary, start a fresh session pointed at a checkpoint file instead of reaching for /compact reflexively.
strategies.expected_benefit: Avoids paying repeated summarization cost on a context that would be cheaper to restart from a written checkpoint.
strategies.drawback: A fresh session pays the full startup floor again with nothing cached yet, so this only wins when you were going to spend even more compacting; a warm mid-session /compact already costs a fraction of what the context size suggests, so this card can be wrong for a session that compacts rarely.
strategies.reversibility: Not applicable, this is a workflow habit.
strategies.how_measured: usage.cache_hit_ratio_median from the profile; a low median hints the cache keeps getting rebuilt, one cause being repeated mid-session compaction. This is a correlational signal, not a direct measurement of compact frequency.
strategies.if_you_say_no: Nothing breaks; compact still works, this is only a suggestion to compare against a fresh session at real boundaries.

strategies.title: Bound reads and search before you read
strategies.what_it_changes: Use Read with offset and limit on large files, and grep or search for the symbol first, instead of reading a whole file to find one thing.
strategies.expected_benefit: Cuts redundant tokens spent re-reading content that a targeted read or search would have found directly.
strategies.drawback: A bounded read can miss context just outside the window, causing a second read later; net worse than one full read on a small file.
strategies.reversibility: Not applicable, this is a workflow habit.
strategies.how_measured: usage.output_tokens_total is a coarse volume proxy; the profile carries no direct measurement of redundant full-file reads, so this gates on overall activity rather than the behavior itself.
strategies.if_you_say_no: Nothing breaks; large files just keep being read in full where a bounded read or a search would have done the job.

strategies.title: Isolate huge tool output instead of inlining it
strategies.what_it_changes: Route build, test, or log output that is mostly noise through a filter or a file instead of letting it land raw in the transcript.
strategies.expected_benefit: Keeps large, low-signal tool output from inflating every later call that re-reads the conversation.
strategies.drawback: Isolating output can hide a detail you needed to see directly; only worth it for logs that are mostly noise, not ones you are actively debugging line by line.
strategies.reversibility: Fully reversible, stop filtering and read raw output again.
strategies.how_measured: usage.output_tokens_total is a coarse volume proxy for how much tool output exists; the profile carries no direct per-tool-call size measurement.
strategies.if_you_say_no: Large tool output keeps landing in the transcript raw and gets re-read on every later call in the session.

strategies.title: Trim an oversize user-level CLAUDE.md
strategies.what_it_changes: Trim the user-level CLAUDE.md toward the documented under-200-lines target; move project-specific or rarely-needed rules into per-project or path-scoped files instead.
strategies.expected_benefit: A smaller user CLAUDE.md is a smaller fixed floor paid on every session, in every project, not just this one.
strategies.drawback: CLAUDE.md loads in full regardless of length, so shrinking it does not change per-call truncation risk the way MEMORY.md does; the saving here is purely the extra tokens re-read as part of the startup floor, and cutting a rule you actually needed loses it everywhere until restored.
strategies.how_measured: instruction.claude_md_user_bytes from the profile, the byte size of the user-level CLAUDE.md.
strategies.if_you_say_no: The full file keeps loading and being re-read as part of the floor on every session, in every project.

strategies.title: Companion: ponytail (build-the-minimum bias)
strategies.what_it_changes: Turn on the ponytail skill, which enforces a build-the-minimum ladder (reuse before writing, stdlib before a dependency, one line before ten) on every response.
strategies.expected_benefit: Less generated code and config to load and re-read later; smaller diffs, fewer new files.
strategies.drawback: It is a behavioral bias, not a check: on a task that genuinely needs the fuller version, a lazy first pass can undershoot and need a second pass, which costs more than building it properly once.
strategies.reversibility: Fully reversible, disable it any time.
strategies.how_measured: instruction.claude_md_project_bytes from the profile; a heavier project instruction file correlates with more built-up scope in general, a loose proxy rather than a direct measurement of code volume.
strategies.if_you_say_no: No change; you keep whatever default building style you already have.

strategies.title: Companion: caveman (terse narration)
strategies.what_it_changes: Turn on the caveman skill to compress narration and status lines into ultra-terse output.
strategies.expected_benefit: Cuts output tokens spent on narration and status commentary.
strategies.drawback: Net-negative risk: a compressed instruction can be misread, causing a corrective turn; if corrective turns rise after enabling it, the extra back-and-forth can cost more than the compression saved. Worth checking, not assuming.
strategies.reversibility: Fully reversible, turn it off any time.
strategies.how_measured: usage.output_tokens_total from the profile; more output volume is where compression has more to work with, a loose proxy rather than a direct narration measurement.
strategies.if_you_say_no: Output stays in full prose; no risk, no saving either.

strategies.title: Companion: token-saver (detect and measure only)
strategies.what_it_changes: Detect-and-measure only: token-saver is already enforced by its own hook when installed, so this card surfaces that its compression is active, it never turns anything on and is never offered as a recommended fix.
strategies.expected_benefit: Visibility into how much shell and tool output volume the plugin is already compressing.
strategies.drawback: This card never recommends installing or enabling token-saver as a fix; its file_content and env processors carry a real redaction risk when enabled and stay out of scope for a detect-only card.
strategies.reversibility: Not applicable, detection only, nothing is changed.
strategies.how_measured: usage.output_tokens_total from the profile, a proxy for how much command output volume exists to compress.
strategies.if_you_say_no: No effect either way; this card only reports, it never changes anything.
